newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries at session highs at midday.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries at session highs at midday.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices rose to session highs at midday after a series of bond friendly economic reports cleared the way for buyers, analysts said.

Beginning with more favorable than anticipated wholesale price and retail sales data on Wednesday and continuing with benign reports on consumer prices and industrial output on Thursday, the market has taken a breather from the selling that had characterized trading for about a week and a half.
At 1210 EDT/1610 GMT, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up 25/32 to 97-17/32, yielding 6.56 percent.
Bargain-hunting overnight set the tone for a firm opening in New York, traders said.
Then the government reported that the July Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.2 percent and that the CPI excluding its food and energy items rose by the same amount.
Coming after very subdued 0.1 percent CPI gains in June, the July report presented a picture of continued subdued inflation, said David Sloan, senior economist at I.D.E.A.
Meanwhile, the Labor Department reported that new jobless claims for the week ended August 9 rose to 316,000 from a revised 304,000. The figure was right in line with forecasts.
Business inventories were reported to have risen 0.7 percent in June, slightly above Reuters' 0.6 percent consensus forecast. Those data had no impact, traders said.
Toward mid-morning, the Federal Reserve reported that industrial production rose 0.2 percent in July as capacity utilization fell to 83.1 percent from a downward revised 83.3 percent in June.

The production increase was exactly in line with economists' forecasts. But the drop in the portion of the nation's mines, utilities and factories employed in that production increase was friendly news for bonds, traders said.
With the data disseminated, the Treasury market remained higher. The benchmark 30-year bond was up about 1/2 a point for much of the morning.
Toward midday, the market's ability to retain its firmer tone encouraged fresh buying and prices rose to session highs.
Analysts at Standard & Poor's MMS said stops were hit as the September T-bond futures contract broke through resistance at 113-19. The 30-year bond also advanced.
"The strength is also dollar related but it's also very technical in nature," said one trader. "It's in thin volume and we're running some stops up here at the 113-20 level."
The dollar was stronger in New York, especially against the yen.
In early afternoon trade, three-month bill rates were up two basis points to 5.19 percent. Six-month bills were unchanged at 5.20 percent. Year bill rates were down two basis points to 5.26 percent.
Two-year notes were up 3/32 to 99-31/32, yielding 5.89 percent. Five-year notes were up 7/32 to 99-16/32, yielding 6.16 percent. Ten-year notes were up 17/32 to 98-30/32, yielding 6.27 percent.
